inputs-en.title: What plants need
inputs-en.goal: Plants need carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil to make food.
inputs-en.checkQuestion: What two things does a plant take in to make its food, and where does each come from?
inputs-en.successCriteria: Names carbon dioxide (from the air, through the leaves or stomata) and water (from the soil, through the roots).
inputs-en.source: Photosynthesis is the process plants use to make their own food. Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air through small openings in their leaves called stomata, and water from the soil through their roots.

green-en.title: Why leaves are green
green-en.goal: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light and reflects green light.
green-en.successCriteria: Says chlorophyll reflects green light (and absorbs mostly red and blue light), so green light reaches our eyes.
green-en.source: Chloroplasts contain a green pigment called chlorophyll, which absorbs energy from sunlight. Chlorophyll absorbs mostly red and blue light and reflects green light, which is why leaves look green.

density-math-en.title: Calculating density
density-math-en.goal: Use rho = m / V and compare with water (1 g/cm3) to predict floating.
density-math-en.checkQuestion: An object has a mass of 30 g and a volume of 10 cm3. What is its density, and will it float in water?
density-math-en.successCriteria: Density is 3 g/cm3, and it sinks because 3 is more than water's 1 g/cm3.
density-math-en.source: Density tells us how much mass is packed into a given volume: rho = m / V. An object floats in water if its density is lower than the density of water, 1 g/cm3.

evaporation-he.title: התאדות
evaporation-he.goal: השמש מחממת את המים, והמים מתאדים והופכים לאדי מים שעולים לאוויר.
evaporation-he.checkQuestion: מה קורה למים בים כשהשמש מחממת אותם?
evaporation-he.successCriteria: אומר שהמים מתאדים או הופכים לאדי מים (גז) שעולים לאוויר.
evaporation-he.source: השמש מחממת את המים בים ובאגמים, והמים מתאדים והופכים לאדי מים.

floating-fr.title: Pourquoi le bois flotte
floating-fr.goal: Un objet flotte si sa masse volumique est plus petite que celle de l'eau.
floating-fr.checkQuestion: Pourquoi le bois de pin flotte-t-il sur l'eau ?
floating-fr.successCriteria: Dit que la masse volumique du pin (environ 0,5 g/cm³) est plus petite que celle de l'eau (1 g/cm³).
floating-fr.source: Un objet flotte dans l'eau si sa masse volumique est plus petite que celle de l'eau, qui vaut 1 g/cm³. Le bois de pin a une masse volumique d'environ 0,5 g/cm³ : il flotte.
